biography: Carlos Augusto Falletti, born in the vibrant heart of São Paulo, Brazil, was practically raised on the roar of engines. His father, a mechanic at Interlagos, would bring young Carlos to the track, where he'd spend hours mesmerized by the speed and spectacle. Carlos began his racing journey in karting at the age of 12, quickly displaying a natural talent and an audacious driving style that earned him both wins and the occasional reprimand. Funding his early career through sheer determination and the unwavering support of his family, Carlos made the leap to single-seaters, where his flashy personality and aggressive maneuvers both thrilled fans and frustrated rivals. A defining moment came in the Brazilian Formula 3 championship when, despite starting last due to a mechanical failure, he clawed his way to victory with a breathtaking last-lap overtake. Now, at 30, Carlos is at the peak of his career, driving for the Privateer Sport team. While a factory seat has eluded him thus far, his raw talent and undeniable charisma make him a constant threat and a fan favorite.
drivingStyle: Falletti's driving style is best described as 'controlled chaos.' He possesses an uncanny ability to extract maximum performance from his car, often flirting with the limits of grip. He's known for his late-braking maneuvers and audacious overtakes, particularly at corners where others fear to tread. While his aggression sometimes leads to costly mistakes, it's also what makes him so exciting to watch. He's a master of tire management, capable of pushing hard when necessary while also nursing his rubber to the finish line. Under pressure, Carlos thrives, often delivering his best performances when the stakes are highest.

careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead at the Monaco Grand Prix in 2022 due to a misjudgment, costing him a potential podium finish and severely damaging his team's morale.
